title: Outcome Summary Record
body:
Overview

This record documents Outcome Summary Record within the Operational Lessons and After-Action Database. Turns documented outcomes into traceable improvements, procedures and training scenarios. It gives the archive a reusable, checkable entry for one recurring task: the entry states what the task is, how it is done, and what result was measured or computed when the accompanying demo program ran. The record is written so a reader can follow it without any other document open, and so an AI can apply it to a new task of the same shape without guessing at missing steps. Nothing in this record claims more than its demo and its stated checks support.

How it works

The method in each record turns an outcome into an improvement with a traceable chain: what happened, what was learned, what action was assigned, and how the improvement was verified. A lesson counts as closed only when its action is done and its verification is recorded; otherwise it stays open and visible.

Worked detail

The worked detail for this entry is concrete. The demo program that accompanies this record ran at build time and produced a real, checkable result, beginning with: actions: 5. The full program and its complete output are shown with this record, so any reader can re-run the same code and confirm the same result. Where the entry involves a judgment, such as which option to prefer or which threshold to use, the judgment and its reasons are stated in the record itself rather than left implicit. Where a limit applies, the limit is named alongside the claim it limits, so the record stays honest about the boundary between what is established and what is still a design or a research question.

Use and ladder

A team uses these records so the same lesson is learned once and kept: procedures get revised, training scenarios get built from real outcomes, and repeat findings are caught by the tracker. Teaching ladder: this record is ranked simple. Simple records introduce one idea at a time, compounded records combine ideas into a working procedure, and most-complex records handle the full procedure with its edge cases and limits. Feasibility tier: established. Implementation status: established. When the status is designed, the record offers a design plus an executed demo; deployment is not claimed. Related databases in the network cover neighboring capabilities and are linked from this database page.
demo_code:
# Outcome Summary Record: track lesson actions to closure with verification.
actions = [('revise procedure', True), ('build training scenario', True), ('update checklist', True), ('verify improvement', False), ('share lesson', True)]
done = [name for name, ok in actions if ok]
open_items = [name for name, ok in actions if not ok]
print("actions:", len(actions))
print("closed:", len(done), done)
print("still open:", len(open_items), open_items)
print("closure fraction:", round(len(done) / len(actions), 3))
print("lesson closed:", not open_items)
demo_output:
actions: 5
closed: 4 ['revise procedure', 'build training scenario', 'update checklist', 'share lesson']
still open: 1 ['verify improvement']
closure fraction: 0.8
lesson closed: False

fields.closure_rule: closed only when action done and verified
